tasks.short: Set depreciation assumptions and advise management on buying, leasing or disposing of capital assets.

steps.what: Check asset records and export acquisition costs, existing depreciation schedules and asset classes.
Read accounting policy, supplier quotes and technical evidence about asset life and residual value.

loop.input: Accounting policy, supplier quote and asset condition report for one asset.
loop.output: Cited evidence fields for useful life, residual value, lease terms and condition.
loop.check: Require source passages; validate amounts, dates and units; the controller checks material interpretations.
loop.stop: At most two extraction attempts per document; missing or conflicting evidence returns to the controller.
loop.why_not_simpler: Technical reports and quotes express relevant facts in inconsistent free text.

steps.what: Determine proposed useful lives, residual values, depreciation methods and policy departures.
Calculate purchase, lease and disposal scenarios, including cash flows and accounting effects.
Discuss operational trade-offs and recommend buying, leasing, retaining or disposing of the asset.
Approve depreciation assumptions and the asset recommendation within delegated authority.
Enter approved depreciation assumptions and retain the approval reference in the asset register.

tasks.design: Configure asset exports and approved depreciation updates in the {ERP}, linked to approval records in the {WORKFLOW}. A calculator on the {DATA_PLATFORM} produces asset comparisons, while a bounded extraction loop turns evidence in the {DOCS} into cited fields. The controller determines assumptions and recommendations; the finance manager approves them before records change.
tasks.previous_blocker: Asset accounting was partly supported by existing software, but technical evidence, scenario workbooks and approval records remained separate.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing asset configuration and deterministic financial calculations cover much of the paperwork. AI coding can shorten implementation, and bounded extraction can handle varied documents without deciding accounting estimates.
tasks.still_hard: Useful life, residual value, impairment indicators and operational alternatives require judgement. Accounting and tax treatment vary by jurisdiction, and old asset records may need substantial cleanup.
tasks.human_edge: The controller connects financial estimates to physical condition, operational needs and defensible accounting treatment.

ambition.what: Monthly equipment replacement review using refreshed purchase, lease and retention scenarios.

tasks.altitude: The controller spends less time assembling evidence and recalculating comparisons, and more time testing assumptions with operational managers. Accounting and spending approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Compare the cash consequences of buying and leasing equipment.
reach.learn: Discounted cash flow, sensitivity analysis and the distinction between cash costs and accounting charges.

reach.task: Review asset estimates during the financial close.
reach.learn: Asset-register controls, estimate-change documentation and reconciliation to the general ledger.

evidence.claim: Asset modules commonly calculate depreciation once approved methods and assumptions are entered.
Purchase and lease comparisons can use deterministic calculations; selecting assumptions remains a judgement task.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates rather than measured outcomes.

assumptions: The company holds operational assets rather than managing investment funds.
The {ERP} contains an asset register with usable exports and an approved update mechanism.
A finance manager approves material estimate changes and asset recommendations within delegated limits.
Build ranges cover a pilot for one entity and a limited set of asset classes, using existing infrastructure.
GDPR applies where evidence contains personal data; EU AI Act applicability depends on the implemented use.
The access range includes checking consultation requirements under national rules; a formal consultation process may take longer.
unknowns: The accounting framework, tax jurisdictions and approved depreciation policies.
Asset-register completeness and available {ERP} configuration, interfaces and licences.
Approval thresholds and who can approve estimate changes and capital decisions.
Availability and reliability of residual-value, maintenance and condition evidence.
Whether personal data or changes to employee working practices trigger consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which accounting and tax requirements govern depreciation estimates and lease treatment in the relevant jurisdictions?
Which condition and resale benchmarks are credible for the asset classes being reviewed?
new_work: Review extracted evidence and resolve conflicting technical or contractual statements.
Maintain approved calculation rules, assumptions and accounting-policy versions.
Investigate rejected updates and reconcile asset changes to approval records.
Validate scenario calculations when tax rules, lease terms or accounting policies change.

tasks.short: Develop staff capability in budgeting and financial management through training, practice and coaching.

steps.what: Review budget errors, recurring finance questions and previous training completion records.
Agree learning objectives and practical priorities with team leads.
Prepare policy explanations, worked examples and budgeting exercises.

loop.input: Training plan, approved finance policy passages and approved financial examples.
loop.output: Draft explanations, exercises and facilitator notes with policy references.
loop.check: Calculate answer keys deterministically; check policy references and figures; the controller approves teaching content.
loop.stop: At most two drafts per module; unresolved policy gaps or numerical mismatches return to the controller.
loop.why_not_simpler: Explanations and exercises need adaptation to learners' questions and experience; calculations need no model.

steps.what: Arrange sessions, enrol attendees and send invitations and preparation materials.
Lead the workshop, explain financial concepts and respond to staff questions.
Guide budgeting exercises and discuss participants' reasoning and mistakes.
Record verified attendance and completion against training enrolments.
Coach staff on applying the learning to their next budget or financial decision.

tasks.design: A small dashboard in the {BI} combines agreed training indicators from the {ERP} and {LMS}, while configured enrolment and calendar flows handle administration. Templates and deterministic exercise calculations support a bounded drafting loop using approved policies in the {DOCS}; the controller approves materials before publication. Workshops, interpretation of mistakes and coaching stay with the controller.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training preparation depended on the controller's experience, while enrolments, examples and follow-up records were maintained separately. Existing learning tools handled administration more readily than relevant finance teaching.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing learning configuration can automate enrolment and completion records. Faster coding makes reusable exercise calculators and data connections cheaper, while bounded drafting helps adapt approved material.
tasks.still_hard: Staff may understand an example but struggle to apply it under pressure. Teaching must reflect local finance policies, protect confidential information and support questions that participants hesitate to ask.
tasks.human_edge: The controller notices confusion, builds confidence and explains how financial choices affect participants' actual work.

ambition.what: A first-budget workshop for newly appointed budget owners before their initial submission.

tasks.altitude: The controller spends less time rewriting examples and arranging sessions, leaving more time for exercises and targeted coaching. Financial approval rights remain unchanged; training priorities stay within the existing mandate.

reach.task: Turn recurring submission errors into practical budgeting exercises.
reach.learn: Budget validation rules, variance interpretation and how to distinguish policy confusion from data problems.

reach.task: Build a training-needs view from aggregated finance and completion data.
reach.learn: Metric definitions, data lineage and privacy-preserving aggregation.

evidence.claim: Learning systems commonly support enrolment, reminders and completion records through configuration.
Deterministic exercise calculators and reusable templates can reduce preparation while live teaching remains human.
Bounded drafting can adapt approved material, but finance-policy accuracy and teaching quality require review.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates rather than measured outcomes.

assumptions: The company has recurring budgeting training and an existing {LMS}, or equivalent training records.
Training materials use approved, anonymised or synthetic financial examples.
Training indicators guide course planning rather than automated employment or performance decisions.
Build ranges cover one training programme and one finance-data connection.
GDPR governs employee training records; EU AI Act applicability depends on whether the use extends into employment assessment.
The access range includes employee or works-council consultation where national rules require it; formal proceedings may extend the schedule.
unknowns: Existing training audiences, session frequency and the controller's actual preparation burden.
Available {LMS} scheduling, attendance and completion features.
Quality and permitted use of budget-error and finance-question records.
Whether training records feed appraisal, promotion or other employment decisions.
Applicable national consultation requirements and existing employee-representative agreements.
Whether the controller has authority and capacity to offer a first-budget workshop.
research_questions: Which national rules govern consultation and reuse of employee learning records?
Which practical assessment methods best show transfer from a finance workshop to budgeting work?
new_work: Review drafted explanations, policy references and exercise answer keys before publication.
Refresh training material when finance policies or budgeting processes change.
Resolve scheduling, attendance and enrolment exceptions.
Maintain data mappings and access controls for training indicators.
Evaluate whether participants apply the learning and adjust exercises accordingly.

role.altitude: The role shifts some effort from assembling financial evidence and training materials to discussing asset choices and developing budget owners. Existing accountability for accounting estimates, financial advice and approvals continues.
reach: Financial analysts' purchase and lease scenario work.
Accountants' asset-estimate reviews and close controls.
Budget analysts' submission quality and variance interpretation.
Business intelligence analysts' governed finance reporting.
skills_to_grow: Financial scenario modelling and sensitivity analysis.
Data lineage, integration requirements and calculation validation.
Review of cited model outputs and handling of exceptions.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a monthly equipment replacement review and a first-budget workshop, supported by reusable calculations and approved evidence. Management can delegate additional authority separately; the tools do not grant it.
